clue.text: Makes certain runs with ease, without a mishap

indicators.note: a mishap throws things into disorder, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letter A, which 'without' says to leave out of the mix

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees an easy run, avoiding any accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' removes an A from RUNS plus EASE, and 'mishap' rearranges the remaining letters RUNSESE.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to see that it happens, which is what making certain means.

clue.text: Odd time gain many find puzzling

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters are in a strange order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: A strange gain in time that many people find hard to explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges TIMEGAIN to ENIGMATI, and C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious or hard to fathom is enigmatic.

clue.text: Suffocates in beastly joints

definitions.meaning: the knee joints in the hind legs of horses and other animals

explanation.surface: Something smothers inside animal joints.
explanation.walkthrough: A stifle is the joint between thigh and lower leg in a horse or dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother someone is to choke them, and the hind-leg knee of a horse also has this name.

clue.text: Meat and drink-an afterthought to, poor Kate

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
PS, the postscript added to a letter

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of meat and drink, plus a postscript to poor Kate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges KATE into TEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarter, this is a familiar kind of meat.

clue.text: Concessions made in work aboard, apparently

indicators.note: in places the work inside the ship letters

parts.note: aboard means on a steamship, abbreviated SS
op, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Concessions made while working on board, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: SS (steamship) is the crossword's ship, so being aboard is being inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sops are small concessions offered to placate someone.

clue.text: Dramatist, lexicographer — or' spider?

definitions.meaning: John ... wrote The Duchess of Malfi
a playful coinage: one who weaves a web, like a spinster spins

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a figure was a playwright, a dictionary-maker or an arachnid.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: two famous bearers of the surname, then a joke reading of the word as 'web-maker', the -ster ending as in spinster.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacobean playwright John and dictionary compiler Noah share the surname, and a spider weaves webs.

clue.text: Their cricketers give quarter to batting side, possibly

parts.note: west is a quarter of the compass
a side batting in cricket is in

indicators.note: possibly says the following word is one arrangement among several

explanation.surface: Cricketers give no mercy to the team batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SIDE into DIES. The Caribbean side play cricket as one team.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean nations field a single combined cricket team, so the cricketers are theirs.

clue.text: Kipling's last work?

definitions.meaning: Kipling's poem of marching soldiers, with its refrain of footwear 'movin' up and down again'
what a cobbler makes on a last, a shoemaker's foot-shaped block

explanation.surface: A query whether a piece was Kipling's final work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like 'final'; it is the cobbler's wooden form.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem has that title, and footwear is made on a shoemaker's last.

clue.text: It runs behind' the tower

parts.note: a vehicle that is towed: it rolls along after whatever is towing it, the tower being one that tows

explanation.surface: Something running behind a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' reads as a tall building; it is one who tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled unit hitched to a car follows behind the vehicle pulling it.

clue.text: What anglers have the right to fish ?

parts.note: eels are fish

explanation.surface: Asking what fishermen have: the right to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers wind their line on a spool attached to the rod.

clue.text: Dialect for love in backward French region

indicators.note: the zero for love goes inside the turned region name
backward tells us the region's name is read from right to left

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A regional way of speaking is described as love found in some part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns MIDI into IDIM, and O goes between its I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a local form of speech, and an idiom can mean a people's particular language or turn of phrase.

clue.text: Music supplied by clergy, man, and drink

parts.note: the comma split aside, a clergyman is a pastor
ale is a drink, a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A list of who supplied the music: a churchman and something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma cuts 'clergyman' in two to make the surface read as a list; read as one word it is PASTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a musical piece evoking rural, shepherd life.

clue.text: Annoy underground worker, a very good man

parts.note: a mole digs tunnels underground
a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Bothering a digger who happens to be a fine fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or bother someone is the older sense of the verb, still used for harassing.

clue.text: Meat dish is beginning to simmer in parts

indicators.note: in places the short pieces inside the actors' parts

parts.note: roles are parts played by actors
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks out just the opening letter of simmer

explanation.surface: A recipe step: a meat dish is starting to simmer in its separate pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like portions of the dish; it means roles in a play. 'beginning to' takes only the first letter of 'simmer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rissoles are fried cakes of minced meat, a kitchen staple.

clue.text: Girl changed date with scholar, meeting painter

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: changed means the letters of date are altered in order

parts.note: MA, a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A girl rearranged a date with an academic, meeting an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns DATE into TADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Alma-Tadema was a Victorian artist known for scenes of the ancient world.

clue.text: Sense which Jaques's man finally lacked

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, alongside sight and hearing
in As You Like It, Jaques's seven ages speech ends with man 'sans teeth, sans eyes, sans' this, 'sans everything'

explanation.surface: Something a character in Shakespeare's speech lost at the end of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of savouring flavours is one of the senses, and it is listed among what old age strips away in the speech.

clue.text: Oviparous beetles spotted?

parts.note: egg-laying spotted beetles, with a hint that female birds also lay eggs

explanation.surface: A naturalist's query about egg-laying spotted insects.
explanation.walkthrough: The beetles are red with black spots; split in two the name is female birds, which are egg-layers too.
explanation.definitionFit: These small domed beetles with spotted wing cases lay eggs, as birds of either kind do.

clue.text: Edward's princely habit of extortion ?

definitions.meaning: Edward the Black Prince's armour, his mail

explanation.surface: The prince Edward made a habit of extracting money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means clothing: the armour of Edward, known as the Black Prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracting money by threats has this name, and the Black Prince's chain armour can be read the same way.

clue.text: Time perhaps to cut things down

definitions.text: Time perhaps to cut things down

parts.words: Time perhaps to cut things down
parts.note: Father Time carries a blade for mowing, so he is one who cuts things down

explanation.surface: It may be time to reduce spending.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Time is pictured carrying a long curved blade for mowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower with a curved long-handled blade is the role Father Time is drawn in.

clue.text: Rebuke officer for happening on board

parts.note: to check someone is to reprove them
a mate is a ship's officer

explanation.surface: A captain reprimands his ship's officer for something that happened aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, with the mate as its officer, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The game-ending position in chess is an event on the chequered board.

clue.text: German prince making mark of the cross

definitions.meaning: a prince entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor
a voter marks a ballot with an X

explanation.surface: A German prince makes the sign of the cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mark of the cross' suggests religion; it is the X on a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in an election, and a prince of the Holy Roman Empire with a vote for the emperor.

clue.text: Monkhouse's theatre ?

definitions.meaning: the ... Theatre is Ireland's national theatre in Dublin

explanation.surface: It reads as asking which theatre belongs to someone called Monkhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkhouse looks like a surname, as of the comedian Bob Monkhouse; taken literally it is a home for monks.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery church and its community form a monks' house, and Dublin's national playhouse bears the same name.

clue.text: Artillery to charge ?

explanation.surface: Guns ready to charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of guns and a legal charge of assault share this word, as does a store of electrical charge.

clue.text: Bird stalked on field?

definitions.meaning: a small songbird of open country
what grows on a stalk in a cornfield: the grain head of a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A bird was followed stealthily across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stalked' looks like hunting the bird; it means borne on a stalk, the grain head of a cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The songbird shares its name with the seed head of a cereal crop.

clue.text: Uses Oxford rather than Cambridge?

parts.note: taking the ox-ford, a shallow crossing, rather than the cam-bridge means walking through water

explanation.surface: A choice of one university over another.
explanation.walkthrough: The universities break into crossings: a FORD you walk through, a BRIDGE you walk over.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking through shallow water is what crossing a ford involves.

clue.text: Net filled by soldier in rising river

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
filled by puts the soldier inside the net

parts.note: taken as written
GI, an American soldier

explanation.surface: A net filled by a soldier in a rising river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' means reading upwards, applied after 'filled by' has done its work. The Teign is a river in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teign flows through Devon into the English Channel.

clue.text: Drawing a Spithead vessel

parts.note: read as Spit's head, the first letter of spit; Spithead is an anchorage off Portsmouth
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a boat anchored at Spithead, near Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a naval anchorage in the Solent; split, its 'head' gives the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing done quickly is a sketch.

clue.text: Some compost employed as a flower-raiser

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some compost was used to raise flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalk holds a bloom up above the plant.

clue.text: Damage found by term-end ? It could be

indicators.note: could be invites us to try other arrangements of the letters

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Harm discovered at the close of a school term.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TERMEND and IT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A detriment is harm or loss suffered.

clue.text: A ray seen on one side of the ship

definitions.text: on one side of the ship

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A ray of light seen beside a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at right angles to a vessel's keel, level with its middle, lies off to the side.

clue.text: Is angry when this shrub is damaged

indicators.note: is damaged says the letters before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener is cross when a shrub gets harmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is the botanical name for lilac, and is also used for the mock orange bush.

clue.text: A poem set in the isle of an Eastern people

indicators.note: set in places the poem inside the island's name

parts.note: the Isle of Man
a lay is a narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: A poem with its setting on an island, about a people of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' puts the poem inside the island; the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayan describes the people of Malaya, in South-East Asia.
